report.title: NO at CHI: Week 11 Scouting Report
report.summary: Chicago leans on early-down and third-and-long passing, and its defense is strong on third down but softer in the red zone. Blitz pressure on passing downs is the main threat to CHI's third-down rate, so the early-down run game and play action matter most. Special teams favor Chicago, and injury news on both sides centers on the offensive line and the corners.

sections.heading: Opponent offense
sections.body: CHI throws on early downs at a 52.3% dropback rate [oc1] over 478 early-down plays [oc2], and on third-and-long it goes to the air 92.3% of the time [oc3] over only 39 plays [oc4]. Its pass rate over expected of 0.53 [oc5] ranks 6th [oc6] in the league, and its offensive EPA per play of 0.04 [oc7] ranks 10th [oc8]. Swift takes 57.4% of designed carries [oc11] over 270 rushes [oc12], and designed runs go right 54.9% [oc13] of the time versus 35.1% left [oc14]. Play action is on 34.5% of dropbacks [oc15]. Targets concentrate in Burden at 22.5% [oc19], Loveland at 19.5% [oc20] and Odunze at 17.4% [oc21]. CHI converts 45.3% on third down [oc25] over 128 plays [oc26] and scores on 56.8% of red-zone drives [oc23] over 37 drives [oc24].

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: CHI's defense is more efficient against the run than the pass. Opponents average -0.07 EPA per run play [dc1] over 169 carries [dc2], while pass plays come in at -0.02 EPA [dc4] over 299 dropbacks [dc5]. CHI keeps 6.8 defenders in the box on run plays [dc9], so NO should test the run game against that count. Pressure is moderate, with an 8.7% sack rate [dc10] and a 37.1% blitz rate [dc12]. The red zone is a soft spot, with opponents scoring on 56.0% of red-zone drives [dc13] over 25 drives [dc14], ranking 13th [dc15]. Third down is the strength, with opponents converting 22.8% [dc16] on 92 plays [dc17], ranked 1st [dc18]. The red-zone sample is small, so treat it as a trend.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: CHI's kicker C. Santos has made 15 [kc1] of 19 [kc2] field goals, a 78.9% rate [kc3], and is 60.0% [kc4] on 5 [kc5] tries from long range. NO is at 70.6% [kc7] on 17 [kc8] attempts. CHI punts net 43.1 [kc9] yards on 26 [kc10] punts. Only 14.0% [kc12] of 50 [kc13] kickoffs are touchbacks, and CHI kickoff coverage allows 23.0 [kc14] yards on 39 [kc15] returns, so avoid short kicks into that return unit. CHI's special-teams EPA is 0.11 [kc18] per play over 234 [kc19] plays, 3rd in the league [kc20], while NO is at -0.02 [kc21] over 246 [kc22] plays.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: CHI's latest report is from week 9 [ic1] and lists RB Kyle Monangai as Questionable [ic2]. He carries 22.2% [ic3] of team rushes over 270 [ic4] rushes, so a backup would take most of that work. CBs Malik Muhammad [ic5] and Tyrique Stevenson [ic6] are also Questionable, and Muhammad plays 74.7% [ic7] of snaps over 7 [ic8] games. NO's latest report is from week 10 [ic11]. Out are DT Christen Miller [ic12], C Erik McCoy [ic15], T Taliese Fuaga [ic18] and RB CJ Donaldson [ic21]. McCoy plays 96.5% [ic16] of snaps over 8 [ic17] games and Fuaga 100.0% [ic19] over 8 [ic20]. Questionable are CB Martin Emerson [ic22] and RB Travis Etienne [ic25], who carries 18.6% [ic26] of team rushes over 204 [ic27] rushes.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Pass protection against the blitz decides the early game. CHI blitzes on 37.1% of dropbacks [mc1], and NO is missing center Erik McCoy, who averaged 96.5% of snaps [mc2], and tackle Taliese Fuaga, who averaged 100.0% [mc3]. Keep a back or tight end in on obvious passing downs. Third-and-long is the second battle: CHI throws on 92.3% [mc4] of those plays over 39 [mc5], and NO allows 47.0% [mc6] third-down conversions over 117 [mc7]. Bring extra rushers there, but keep the intermediate middle covered given CHI's 10.2% [mc9] explosive pass play rate. Early-down runs set up play action, which CHI uses on 34.5% [mc16] of dropbacks, so stack the right edge and keep linebackers from biting. Take points late and avoid short kicks into CHI's return unit.
